paragraphs.en: Be the first to empty your hand. The whole 52-card deck, without jokers, is dealt as evenly as possible to 2–8 players. The first player is chosen at random. You see your own hand; everyone can read how many cards each player holds by pressing S.

In the default game you play one to four cards face down and declare their rank. The first declaration is aces, followed by twos, threes and so on through ten, jack, queen and king, then back to aces. The actual cards may be different: bluffing is a legal part of the game. The number of cards you play is always announced accurately.

Use Up and Down to move through your whole hand, or Left and Right to jump between suits. H reads your hand in its current display order. You may choose any of your cards, including cards that do not match the declaration.

To play one card, select it and press Enter. For a larger packet, mark cards with Shift+Enter; pressing it again removes a card from the packet. P reads the marked cards and Shift+P clears them. When you press Enter, the card under the cursor is added too if it was not marked. Check the final card count and declaration, then choose Play. Escape or Cancel returns to the hand without playing or clearing your packet. The hand’s context menu also offers Play.

For example, on an ace turn you can select two different cards and declare two aces. Both may be aces, neither may be an ace, or only one may be an ace. Opponents hear the declaration and count, not the hidden card names. Once the reactions finish, the next player declares twos even if someone challenged your aces.

After every face-down play, the other players decide in seat order, starting with the next seat. When your decision is due, press K or choose Challenge to question the play. Press Space or choose Do not challenge to pass this decision to the next opponent. This is not a promise that the cards are true and is not the Bluff variant’s pass.

There is no reaction countdown. Waiting, reading help or leaving the keyboard does not accept the play. Only the player currently asked may respond. The first challenge closes the other reactions. If everyone declines to challenge, the cards stay on the pile and play continues.

A challenge reveals only the latest packet. If even one of its cards has a different rank, its author takes the whole pile. If every card matches, the challenger takes the whole pile. Earlier hidden cards are not revealed merely because the pile is collected. The required rank and next seat continue normally after either outcome. C repeats the public pile size, last declaration and current decision; T says who must act.

Playing your last cards does not immediately win: opponents still get their normal reactions. You win when everyone accepts that play, even if it was a bluff. You also win if a challenge proves your last packet true. If your last bluff is caught, you take the pile and keep playing. The game ends with one winner; the other players receive no points and are not ranked.
Choose Variant when creating the table. Classic: ascending ranks is the default described above. All variants use one deck and the same ordered, untimed reactions.
- Descending ranks starts with aces, then king, queen, jack, ten and down to two, returning to ace. Challenges do not reset this cycle.

- Same or neighbouring rank starts with aces. Afterwards choose the previous declared rank or either neighbour. After seven you can declare six, seven or eight; after ace you can declare king, ace or two. King and ace are neighbours in this version. Select the declaration in the play dialog and choose Play to submit the cards together with it.
- Bluff: fixed pile rank is for 3–6 players and adds passing, explained below.
- Suit: single cards uses a face-up opening and then concealed single cards, explained below.

title.en: Bluff: one rank until the pile closes

paragraphs.en: The opener plays one to four cards and chooses any of the thirteen ranks in the play dialog. That rank applies to every later packet on this pile. On your playing turn, add one to four cards or press X to pass until the pile closes. You cannot open an empty pile by passing.

A pass prevents you from adding more cards to this pile, but you still decide whether to challenge each new packet. Playing another packet does not bring passed players back. If only one player has not passed, that player may keep adding packets; the others still get reactions each time.

When every player has passed, the pile is set aside face down and the last person who played opens a new pile with any rank. After a correct challenge, the challenger opens; after a wrong challenge, the challenged author opens. Passes are then cleared. A last packet must still survive reactions before its author wins. In this version the entire deck is dealt, and neither jokers nor Force rules are used.

title.en: Suit: face-up opening and single cards

paragraphs.en: The opener selects a card and presses Enter to confirm a face-up opening. Its actual suit becomes the pile’s suit. This visible card cannot be challenged. Each following player plays one card face down, declaring that same suit; no rank is declared. Shift+Enter cannot build a multi-card packet here.

Use K or Space when asked about a concealed play. A challenge checks only the suit: a seven and a king of hearts both satisfy a hearts declaration. A wrong suit makes the author collect the pile; a true suit makes the challenger collect it. Whoever collects opens the next pile with any face-up card. If your last card is the face-up opening, you win immediately. A last concealed card must survive reactions as usual.

Dealing uses the shuffle sound, and an accepted play uses the card-placement sound whether it is true or a bluff. A challenge has a distinct signal, followed by reveal, outcome and collection sounds. The usual decision cue tells you when to play or react; the usual result cues mark the end. All important information is also spoken, so the game remains playable with optional effects switched off.
Enter: prepare and confirm the current card or packet
Shift+Enter: mark or unmark the current card, except in Suit
P: read the prepared packet
Shift+P: clear the prepared packet
K: challenge when it is your reaction
Space: decline to challenge this play
X: pass until the pile closes in Bluff
H: read your own hand
T: read who must play or react
S: read each player’s card count
C: read the public pile and declaration
Shift+C: sort by suit
Shift+H: sort by rank
Shift+M: restore acquisition order
Z: move to the next playable card without playing
Shift+Z: move to the previous playable card without playing
Escape: cancel your current choice
